question: Across four new published independent original animal-GPS studies tracking ≥2 native taxa, do recorded NIGHT−DAY displacement niches form source-study-specific rankings on exactly co-observed astronomical dates, and do species contrasts in source-reference photoperiod trends differ across sites and locomotor guilds?
source_selection: Selected solely on fixed public metadata (new DOI+study ID relative to Illinois/Wyoming/Utah temporal comparison; ≥2 distinct registered taxa; GPS source, ≥10 reported animals, ≥150000 original fixes, guild diversity). Includes Galápagos giant tortoises, migratory ducks, African vultures, and grazing geese. Not representative random sampling, and some sources were previously used for solar-direction cataloging, so NOT all-behavior untouched prospective external replication.
independence: Original field-study DOI and repository study ID are the replication units. Exclude a known duplicate DOI for African vultures (10.5441/001/1.pr1vj29n) sharing study ID 2919708. Native taxa within one study are dependent. No claim they were spatially sympatric merely because source calendar dates overlap.

stage1_metadata.execute_before_animal_GPS: Retrieve source ORIGINAL bundle bitstream inventory ONLY. Select a unique original GPS or tracking CSV/CSV.gz/ZIP by filename, never by q or daylength results. Freeze bitstream UUID/bytes/checksum and source metadata status to git before animal event reads.
stage1_metadata.hold_policy: Multiple plausible tracking files, unsupported type, missing provider checksum, no GPS native taxonomy, over 200MB or source API errors -> METADATA_HOLD, never replace study/taxa.
stage1_metadata.original_primary_file_resolution_when_tw: If exactly two otherwise eligible ORIGINAL tracking CSV files coexist, choose the uniquely larger CSV only when it is >=10,000,000 bytes and at least 10 times the other, based strictly on provider names/sizes (before GPS event access). The smaller may be a derived summary; do not open it to choose. Otherwise metadata HOLD. No behavioral content or taxon effect may enter resolution.
stage1_metadata.original_census_pre_event_manifest_repla: Prior source-only first report is superseded BEFORE any original GPS event access; final metadata receipt SHA must be pinned independently. Historical first metadata receipt remains in Git history.

new_event_contract.time: At most one fix per UTC-hour bin from original event timestamps; accepted 0.5 to 2.0 hours between original adjacent fixes, speed <=60 km/h, same local solar date and daypart at begin/mid/end; no interpolation.
new_event_contract.native_day_q: Within original tagged animal×solar date at least 3 accepted DAY and 3 NIGHT GPS movement steps; q=log1p(median NIGHT GPS km/h)-log1p(median DAY GPS km/h), not latent activity hours.
new_event_contract.native_year: For native taxon baseline an animal-year requires ≥10 eligible q days. For source level same-calendar group each native tag/year with >=10 dates in shared source calendar; do not require photoperiod span to estimate q.
new_event_contract.coobserved_source_calendar: All registered taxa >1 are preselected. Iterative fixed-point intersection of eligible source (calendar year, local solar date) across EVERY native taxon; prune tag-years with fewer than 10 common days until stable. Report no-overlap hold, never select best subset of species or pair on q outcome.
new_event_contract.study_reference_daylength: A common STUDY-level astronomical reference latitude from median original valid GPS latitude across all registered source native taxa, computed blind to q/daylength outcome and never published as exact coordinate. This is reference daylength, not each animal's actual exposure (especially migratory species).
new_event_contract.photoperiod: Within each tag-year regression q~common study-reference astronomical daylength across source-shared dates; require ≥10 common days and >=0.5 h observed daylength variation, else SLOPE_UNAVAILABLE. Island/equatorial reference may never meet threshold; do not alter cutoff after seeing this.
new_event_contract.native_bootstrap: For native q positions and q~daylength slope, source group mean over original tagged animals with ≥5 animals required; 2000 fixed-seed animal resamples, nominal 95% interval; record unsupported explicitly.
new_event_contract.pair_q: For EVERY unordered pre-fixed native species pair in source study, compare q levels on source-wide all-taxa shared dates; original tagged animal independent bootstrap across the two taxa; status only if ≥5 tags per side. No multiple-testing adjusted assertions.
new_event_contract.pair_calendar_slope: Native daily q mean over available tagged animals on same source calendar date, pair difference q_A-q_B regressed on study-reference daylength, year-month block bootstrap if >=5 independent year-month blocks and >=40 shared days; additionally within-month demeaning with ≥5 usable blocks and >=0.25h² residual photoperiod variation. Do not interpret as causal daylength.
new_event_contract.source_support: Publish number of distinct source original animals, original valid fix/day counts, shared source date and year-month counts but never original dates, source study coordinates, tag IDs, per-animal observations or timestamps. An unsupported source is not zero.
new_event_contract.inference: Compare source-native niche positions vs seasonal slopes as separate biological axes; species/region/guild/telemetry duty cycle remain confounded. Four purposively selected published studies, not a representative global random sample.

historical: Maintain prior Illinois three-species 169-calendar-date and Wyoming two-species 193-calendar-date original source outputs and all month-adjusted signed/hypothesis limits.
Maintain 48-source signed shortwave-direction heldout negative replication result NOT REPLICATED.
Maintain 12 old ERA5 raw JSON source identity HOLDS and the fact old numerical weather arrays are not archived.
No eBird or TinyFish source access.
